posts.name: wizard
posts.cooked:
• Bots make up a massive portion of the Monthly Active Users (MAU) metric for the shareholders. Banning them, at least before a report period, would be counterproductive to their bottom line.
  • Ban waves take too long to be enacted. It’s highly profitable to create a new account and use a bot to farm gold since they will make far more money than they ever lose, especially in classic where there’s no box price to the game. Gold generation is at an all time high. Blizzard’s answer is to create more gold sinks in the game when in reality there’s too much gold from nefarious sources and the average real player will never be able to collect that much.
  • Gold buying isn’t punished enough. To deter players from buying gold they need to:
    — Ban the gold seller.
    — Delete all gold in the transaction from all sources, even if it’s already changed hands.
    — Ban the gold buyer.
    — Remove any/all achievements, colllectibles, and progress on any associated account. If you’re banned you still keep all of your achievements and collections across your Battlenet account so you don’t really lose too much if you have to make a new WoW license.
  • Set a generic filter in trade chat and LFG that auto bans advertisements of any kind for carries/sales of “services”
  • Set a generic chat filter in LFG and the services channel that auto detects and bans any/all sales that advertise any form of 3rd party (website, discord etc…) entity to discuss payments.
  • Strictly monitor the services channel as it is really just a spam haven for RMT and frauds. There’s almost no legitimate sellers in services, it’s just a wall of RMT spam that is so blatant and obvious. These people need instant account closures.
  • Implement name/payment method/hardware bans on commercial use bots and sellers.
  • Do better at detecting and banning VPNs as this is a main way that these mostly foreign gold sellers access US servers to cheat and sell illegal gold.

There’s so much that could be done, but let’s be real. Blizzard doesn’t want any of it. Banning bots that generate gold would kill token sales and make it impossible for people to legitimately afford things. The mass inflation would go down over night, trade goods would immediately skyrocket in price due to bots not being able to sell them anymore. It’d just be a mess.
